title: Function notation, domain, range
examples: What does the notation f of x mean?
How do I find the domain of a function?
Can a function have a restricted domain?

explain.say: Today we look at function notation. It is a way to write a rule for a relationship. We write it as f of x. This means the function takes an input x. For example, if the rule is multiply by two, we write f of x equals 2x. The input x goes into the rule. The output is what comes out.

items: Input x goes into the rule

explain.say: The input is the value we put into the function. We call this the domain. Think of it like the ingredients you can use. If the function is f of x equals x minus three, and we use an input of five, we write f of five. We substitute five for x. So, f of five equals five minus three, which is two. Two is our output.

The range is the set of all possible outputs. It tells us what answers the function can give. If our function is f of x equals x squared, the output can never be a negative number. The range is all numbers greater than or equal to zero. The domain might be all real numbers.

items: y ≥ 0: All numbers greater than or equal to zero

explain.say: Sometimes we must consider restrictions on the domain. A common restriction is dividing by zero. If we have f of x equals one divided by x minus four, we cannot let x equal four. If x equals four, the function is undefined. So, four is excluded from the domain.

faq.q: What is the difference between the domain and the range?
faq.a: The domain is the set of all possible inputs you can use. The range is the set of all possible outputs the function can produce. You can think of the domain as the allowed inputs and the range as the resulting outputs.
asks: What values can the function give?

faq.q: If I see f of x equals x plus one, what is the domain?
faq.a: For this simple function, you can use any real number as an input. Therefore, the domain is all real numbers. You can always add one to any number.
asks: Can I use any number for x?
Is there any restriction on the inputs?

faq.q: How do I find the range when I have a square root function?
faq.a: The square root symbol always gives a non-negative result. This means the output, or range, must be zero or positive. The range is usually greater than or equal to zero.
asks: What is the smallest possible output?
Does the range start at zero?

faq.q: What is the most common restriction I should look out for?
faq.a: The most common restriction is when you have a variable in the denominator. You must ensure that the denominator does not equal zero. Setting the denominator to zero tells you the value to exclude.
asks: When can I not divide by?

faq.q: Does the notation f of x mean something else?
faq.a: No, f of x is just the name we give to the function rule. It is a placeholder for the relationship between the input and the output. It does not change what the function actually does.
asks: Is f of x just a name?

facts: The domain is the set of all permissible inputs for a function.
The range is the set of all possible outputs from a function.
When dealing with fractions, the denominator cannot equal zero.
A function rule can be written using the notation f of x.

quiz.say: What is the domain of f(x) equals one divided by x?
quiz.why: You cannot divide by zero, so zero must be excluded from the inputs.

wrong.0: This suggests the restriction is at one, not zero.
wrong.2: This incorrectly includes zero as a possible input.
wrong.3: This incorrectly excludes negative numbers as inputs.

quiz.say: For f(x) equals the square root of x, what is the possible range?
quiz.why: The square root symbol by itself always produces a non-negative output.

wrong.0: This describes the domain, not the range of outputs.
wrong.1: This incorrectly excludes the possibility of the output being exactly zero.
wrong.3: This incorrectly suggests negative outputs are possible.
